# Platinum: EOS reconstruction reports

<!-- Generated by scripts.generate_reconstruction_reports; edit EOSMAT instead. -->

[All reconstruction reports](index.md) · [Material and EOS parameters](../material-summaries/platinum.md) · [EOSMAT record file](https://github.com/CPrescher/peritheos/blob/main/peritheos/data/materials/platinum.eosmat) · [Audit sidecar](https://github.com/CPrescher/peritheos/blob/main/peritheos/data/audits/platinum.audit.json)

Each section opens with the record's reproduction headline and any usage
warning ([label definitions](../eos-labels.md)), then the scope and basis of
the stored check. Only recorded content is shown: missing selections, weights,
errors or conventions are unknown, not zero, and are not inferred. Generating
this page fits nothing and changes no classification or source coefficient.
Every record is also listed by identifier in the
[numerical ledger](../primary-eos-refits.md#records), its
[machine-readable form](https://github.com/CPrescher/peritheos/blob/main/docs/data/primary-eos-refits.json) and the
[source-audit reports](../source-audits.md).

**Curves and residuals** replay the full stored source and reconstructed
coefficients on the same recorded audit inputs. Residual = model − input in
the fitted quantity's native units; for pressure, P(model) − P(input) at each
input volume and temperature (isothermal records use their reference
temperature). RMS is an unweighted descriptive error, not a parameter
uncertainty or the weighted fitting objective. With more than five
temperatures, the minimum, middle and maximum isotherms are drawn; residuals
include every selected row. Error bars appear only where all widths are
recoverable and keep the source meaning, including digitization widths.
No uncertainty band is inferred.

**Coefficient graphs** show stored central values and recorded error widths
in the audit's units; each panel includes zero. They are not observation or
residual plots. Fixed/adopted values are constraints, not recovered values.
Tables round an error to two significant digits when its leading digit is 1
or 2, otherwise one, and the value to the error's decimal place; values
without a positive error show at most six significant digits. Full precision
stays in EOSMAT and the ledger.

<a id="record-platinum_holmes_1989_vinet_1"></a>

## Holmes et al. (1989), theoretical 300 K Vinet scale

**untested** (not refittable) · `platinum_holmes_1989_vinet_1` · `Vinet` · [Coefficients and source](../material-summaries/platinum.md#record-platinum_holmes_1989_vinet_1)

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization. **Basis:** Equation (11) and Table IV make the published 300 K Vinet curve exactly reconstructable, but the source does not tabulate its LMTO E0(V), P0(V), density-of-states, or 300 K fit grid. The bundled Table III rows are shock-Hugoniot qualification experiments and must not be fitted as a 300 K isotherm; the source-derived equation checkpoints are circular fit inputs. The underlying theoretical regression therefore remains not independently refittable.

### Method

- **Dataset identifiers:** platinum\_holmes\_1989\_table3\_shock
- **Fixed parameters:** V0

### More evidence

- [Supporting source report: holmes-1989-platinum](../literature-reproductions/holmes-1989-platinum.md).

## Shen and Smith (2026), Cu-referenced Vinet

**reproduced** · `platinum_shen_2026_vinet_2` · `Vinet` · [Coefficients and source](../material-summaries/platinum.md#record-platinum_shen_2026_vinet_2)

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization. **Basis:** Every compared free coefficient meets both the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison and parameter-specific numerical similarity screen. Error conventions and fit qualifications remain applicable.

- Direct reconstruction from source observations: each Table S1 phase volume is paired with its simultaneous Cu volume, pressure is evaluated from Fratanduono et al.'s analytic third-order 298 K Vinet fit, and K0 and K0\_prime are fitted with Shen and Smith's fixed V0 and stated run selection. The source publishes no pressure weights, residual covariance, or weighting protocol, so the reproduction uses unweighted pressure residuals and does not infer any of them.

### Method

- **Dataset identifiers:** shen\_smith\_2026\_table\_s1\_simultaneous\_volumes
- **Observations:** 387
- **Fit kind:** fixed\_v0\_vinet\_with\_reconstructed\_cu\_pressure
- **Selection:** Pt; DAC-2
- **Objective:** unweighted\_pressure\_residuals
- **Absolute sigma:** False
- **Free parameters:** K0; K0\_prime
- **Fixed parameters:** V0

<a id="record-platinum_dorogokupets_oganov_2007_vinet_4"></a>

## Dorogokupets and Oganov (2007), Vinet four-oscillator thermal scale

**untested** (not refittable) · `platinum_dorogokupets_oganov_2007_vinet_4` · `Vinet` · [Coefficients and source](../material-summaries/platinum.md#record-platinum_dorogokupets_oganov_2007_vinet_4)

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization. **Basis:** The 36 bundled Dewaele static rows are a recoverable stage-2 subset, and the seven Holmes shots are an independent Equation-15 diagnostic. The published result is nevertheless a two-stage weighted optimization of six metals: the complete observation inventory and weights, selected Shock Wave Database rows, Collard-McLellan Figure 1 K\_S(T) coordinates, and platinum-specific thermochemical row mapping are not published. The dedicated audit therefore validates exact calculated outputs and partial source subsets without claiming a numerical reconstruction of the global objective.

### Method

- **Dataset identifiers:** platinum\_dewaele\_2004\_table1\_compression; platinum\_holmes\_1989\_table3\_shock

### More evidence

<a id="record-platinum_sokolova_2013_holzapfel_3"></a>

## Sokolova et al. (2013), Holzapfel thermal (2016 workbook)

**untested** (source calculation reconstructed) · `platinum_sokolova_2013_holzapfel_3` · `Holzapfel` · [Coefficients and source](../material-summaries/platinum.md#record-platinum_sokolova_2013_holzapfel_3)

**Scope:** Reconstruction of a source equation or calculation. **Basis:** All eleven machine-readable comparison series enter one shared Equation (20) objective against the mean Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherm. Table 4 is retained as a post-calibration closure test. The calculation cannot recover the eleven EOS parameter sets independently because the source omits complete thermochemical/ultrasonic rows, weights, and covariance.

### Method

- **Dataset identifiers:** platinum\_dewaele\_2004\_table1\_compression
- **Observations:** 35
- **Fit kind:** coupled\_eleven\_marker\_ruby\_cross\_calibration
- **Objective:** minimize the sum over markers of the mean squared residual between Equation (20) and the pointwise mean of the Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet pressures, so each of the eleven markers has equal total weight
- **Fixed parameters:** n; Z; n

Recorded pressure RMS error (GPa), in the audit's own coordinates and objective: source fit 0.529; reconstruction 0.628.

<summary>Recorded diagnostics, covariance and additional protocol</summary>

    - **M:** 6

    - **M:** 6.10335

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization. **Basis:** Agreement within the source's reported parameter error widths; this is not an inferred confidence convention.

- Every compared free central value lies inside its printed source error width, with finite reconstructed standard errors under the explicit conditional error model.
